items.title: Hackers disguise phishing as promising business opportunities
items.summary:
Attackers are breaking into business email accounts with short messages asking whether a company can quote on an upcoming project, the kind of request sales and procurement staff answer every week. Cadence Riddle, a cybersecurity researcher at Fortra, tracked a 12-fold increase in malicious emails mentioning “RFQ” (request for quotation) between October 2025 and September 2026. In nearly 73% of cases, the lure led to a page built to steal login credentials. “RFQ communication is … More →

items.title: Scammers clone candidates’ voices to steal cash and voter data ahead of 2026 midterms, FBI warns
items.summary:
Three weeks before Americans vote in the 2026 midterm election, fraudsters are borrowing candidate names, logos and slogans to collect fake donations and harvest personal data, the FBI warned. “The FBI warns the public that scammers could exploit the 2026 US Midterm Election to perpetrate financial fraud schemes,” reads the public service announcement, which adds that these schemes target victims throughout the country and “have previously exploited state and local elections.” The alert updates a … More →

items.title: Fake Arch Linux AUR packages exploit typos to run malware with root privileges
items.summary:
Arch Linux users who mistyped yay or paru while installing the package helpers from the Arch User Repository (AUR) may have given a stranger root access to their machine. AUR is a popular community package source for Arch Linux and related distributions, hosting user-submitted build scripts for proprietary programs, beta builds and older software versions that the official repositories do not carry. Yay and paru, known as AUR helpers, search the AUR for software and … More →

items.title: The cyber talent shortage? Job postings just hit a four-year low
items.summary:
US employers posted 235,786 cybersecurity jobs from January through September 2026. That is the lowest total for those months in the four years that staffing and workforce intelligence firm CyberSN has tracked. They pulled the listings from job data provider JobSpikr, removed duplicates and sorted each one by the security work it described. The postings that remain have drifted toward governance, risk and compliance (GRC), the teams that track an organization’s risk and answer to … More →

items.title: Stolen AI API keys are paying for hackers’ autonomous scans
items.summary:
A seller on a restricted criminal forum is marketing an autonomous hacking tool that runs on stolen OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys, so the key’s owner pays for the scans. Bitsight’s threat intelligence team tracked the shift across thousands of posts on 16 underground forums from February through August 2026. items.title: DDoS attacks can knock services offline before links reach capacity
items.summary:
More than 9.1 million DDoS attacks were recorded globally between January and June 2026, an increase of nearly a quarter year over year, according to Netscout’s DDoS Threat Intelligence Report. Large attacks and distributed targeting strain defenses Attacks exceeding 1 Tbps or 1 Gpps increased 1,286% year over year. Much of that growth came from botnet operators associated with Aisuru, Kimwolf, Jackskid, and their successors. That means attackers need fewer devices to launch large attacks. … More →
